title: MHFE prototype implementation audit

snapshot.workingTree: No initial commit; all implementation files were untracked. Audit files are excluded from the fingerprint.
snapshot.publicationRelationship: First immutable commit containing all seven verified AUD-001 remediations. AUD-002 independently confirmed their presence there; this does not replace the original pre-commit audit snapshot.

included: BIP39 parsing and universal N-to-24 packing
Feistel, KDF, PRF and inverse wiring
native, CLI, WASM and Worker APIs

checks.evidence: Seventeen fast library tests passed, including literal byte/bit order, UTF-8 validity and preservation, byte-length boundaries, real packed-state detection, and complete ambiguity reporting.
Specification/source comparison and previously completed vector traces; no security proof.
Native/WASM contract review and Chromium byte/module probes.
Locked native and WASM builds plus standalone API check.
11 direct crates.io dependencies, no path/Git dependencies; RustSec reported no advisories across 61 packages.
Recorded real-parameter round trip: 85.337 s encrypt, 84.145 s decrypt.

findings.title: Operational APIs retained unnecessary secret transcripts and lacked systematic best-effort cleanup
findings.reproduction: Inspect the initial operational result and buffer ownership paths.
findings.expected: Routine operations expose only required outputs and release reachable secret buffers on normal disposal.
findings.observed: Early result types exposed plaintext and round transcript material and several owned buffers lacked systematic cleanup.
findings.impact: Consumers could retain substantially more sensitive material than required.
findings.evidence: Final source separates operational and vector-only results and uses zeroize/Zeroizing on reachable owners.
findings.recommendedFix: Separate debug/vector transcripts and apply best-effort cleanup without claiming physical erasure.
findings.requiredVerification: Source trace, API tests and browser disposal checks.

findings.title: Worker-owned WASM loading conflicted with offline single-file integration
findings.reproduction: Initialize the initial Worker in an embedded document with connect-src none.
findings.expected: The Worker starts without network access and signals readiness before operations.
findings.observed: The initial Worker needed to fetch its WASM URL.
findings.impact: Single-file offline consumers could fail or weaken CSP.
findings.evidence: Final Chromium probes passed with caller-supplied WebAssembly.Module and byte initialization.
findings.recommendedFix: Pass compiled modules or bytes through an explicit initialization handshake.
findings.requiredVerification: Byte/module startup, readiness, failure and cancellation probes under offline CSP.

findings.title: Release and WASM crate-type integration initially failed to link cleanly
findings.reproduction: Build clean native release and browser artifacts under the initial combined crate-type setup.
findings.expected: Both native rlib/CLI and WASM cdylib artifacts build from the locked standalone crate.
findings.observed: The initial configuration produced output/link integration failures.
findings.impact: A release could fail despite successful source-level checks.
findings.evidence: Final locked native build, explicit cargo rustc cdylib build, bindings and standalone check passed.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep the reusable native rlib default and request cdylib explicitly in the WASM build.
findings.requiredVerification: Clean native and WASM release builds and generated API verification.

findings.title: Required fixed-point refusal was absent
findings.reproduction: Review encryption completion against the suite requirement for Y equal to X.
findings.expected: A fixed point is refused with a stable error.
findings.impact: A rare fixed point could expose the source as the apparent container.
findings.evidence: The FIXED_POINT path and equality/non-equality unit test pass.
findings.recommendedFix: Compare input and output state before encoding the container.

findings.title: Recovery required an explicit source length instead of implementing the specified automatic detection
findings.reproduction: Inspect the original recovery APIs and observe that source_words was mandatory and only one verifier layout was tested.
findings.expected: After one inverse permutation, every short layout is tested; one match selects it, no match falls back to 24 words, and multiple matches report the complete set.
findings.observed: Automatic detection and ambiguity reporting were absent.
findings.impact: Recovery depended on separately supplied length metadata and could not implement the specification's ambiguity rule.
findings.evidence: The final core, CLI, WASM, and Worker expose automatic recovery; tests cover zero, one, two, three, and four matches and real packed states.
findings.recommendedFix: Implement one complete classifier shared by every automatic recovery adapter while retaining explicit length as an override.
findings.requiredVerification: Fast classifier tests, WASM library compilation, and JavaScript syntax checks.

findings.title: Argon2 work-area allocation could abort instead of returning a typed error
findings.reproduction: Inspect allocation of the 512 MiB Block vector under constrained memory.
findings.expected: Reservation failure reaches the caller as a stable error.
findings.observed: Direct allocation could terminate before structured error handling.
findings.impact: A constrained Worker or CLI could disappear without a useful diagnostic.
findings.evidence: Final source uses fallible reservation and maps MEMORY_ALLOCATION_FAILURE; real host OOM was not induced.
findings.recommendedFix: Reserve fallibly before initializing the KDF work area.
findings.requiredVerification: Error-path unit test or a controlled allocator-failure harness.

findings.title: Worker termination documentation overstated zeroization guarantees
findings.reproduction: Compare the original cancellation claim with browser Worker termination semantics.
findings.expected: Documentation distinguishes reachable-buffer cleanup from guaranteed physical erasure.
findings.observed: Initial wording implied termination runs cleanup and erases memory.
findings.impact: Consumers could rely on a guarantee the browser does not provide.
findings.evidence: Final documentation consistently describes normal disposal and forced termination limitations.

observations.title: Prototype repository has no immutable revision history
observations.evidence: Git reports no HEAD and all implementation paths as untracked.
observations.reproduction: Run git status and git rev-parse HEAD.
observations.expected: Audit evidence is preferably tied to an immutable commit.
observations.observed: Only a manifest fingerprint identifies the reviewed tree.
observations.impact: Later provenance and remediation comparisons are harder.
observations.recommendedFix: Create an initial reviewed commit before publication.
observations.requiredVerification: Record the commit and rerun release gates.

remediation.evidence: Fast classifier, WASM library, and JavaScript checks
Fallible allocation path; real OOM not induced

limitations: No independent cryptography-specialist audit or formal security proof.
No Firefox runtime acceptance, cross-platform release build, Docker run or reproducibility comparison.
The expensive vector replay and full Chromium round trip passed before final cleanup-only and documentation/test edits and were not repeated at the owner's request.
Final fingerprint verification was limited to formatting, seventeen fast library tests, a WASM library check, and JavaScript syntax checks.
